5    Weighted class of currents of relative full mass inter-
     section
In this subsection, we introduce the notion of weighted classes of currents with full mass
intersection relative to a closed positive current T . We only consider convex weights
in the sequel. We refer to [16, 4, 6] for the case where T ≡ 1 and informations on
non-convex weights. We also note that [4] considers currents in big classes whereas our
setting here is restricted to currents in Kähler classes.
    We fix our setting. Let ω be a Kähler form on X. Let m ∈ N∗ . Let Tj = ddc uj + θj be a
closed positive (1, 1)-current where θj is a smooth Kähler form and uj is a negative θj -psh
function for 1 ≤ j ≤ m. Let 0 ≤ p ≤ n be an integer and T a closed positive current
of bi-degree (p, p) on X. We assume p + m ≤ n. This is a minimal assumption because
otherwise the relative non-pluripolar product is automatically zero by a bi-degree reason.
    For k ∈ N, put ujk := max{uj , −k} and Tjk := ddc ujk + θj . Note that Tjk ≥ 0
because θj ≥ 0. Let β be a Kähler (1, 1)-class and Em (β, T ) the set of closed positive

times β). The class En (β) was introduced in [16]. We first prove the following result
giving the convexity of the class of currents of relative full mass intersection.
Theorem 5.1. Assume that Tj , . . . , Tj (m times Tj ) are of full mass intersection relative
to T for 1 ≤ j ≤ m. Then, T1 , . . . , Tm are also of full mass intersection relative to T . In
particular, for Kähler (1, 1)-classes β, β ′ , we have

and Em (β, T ) is convex .

Theorem 5.9. Let χ ∈ W − . Assume that Tj , . . . , Tj (m times Tj ) are of full mass intersection
relative to T with weight χ for 1 ≤ j ≤ m. Then, T1 , . . . , Tm are also of full mass intersection
relative to T with weight χ. In particular, for Kähler (1, 1)-classes β, β ′, we have

                            Eχ,m (β, T ) + Eχ,m(β ′ , T ) ⊂ Eχ,m (β + β ′ , T )

and Eχ,m (β, T ) is convex.
Proof. The second and third desired assertions are direct consequences of the first one.
We prove the first desired assertion. Firstly, by Theorem 5.1, we have

scope_limits: Section5 printed for Kahler current classes and negative absolute potentials. Vu2005.13241v3 Section3 separately treats prescribed references in arbitrary pseudoeffective classes; the translation of any new zero-volume energy application still requires proof.
Proposition5.10 proof is explicitly by reference to BEGZ plus Lemma5.2/Theorem5.8, not a fully printed new continuity proof.
Theorem4.9 requires full mass against the MINIMAL reference class; do not silently substitute arbitrary psi-relative full mass without proving the variant.
The definition of relative minimal-product classes in Vu4 differs from BEGZ limiting positive products outside big classes; Question4.7 explicitly retains that distinction.

Printed Lemma5.7 Eq5.13 has a plus sign where smooth Stokes gives a minus; the valid chain rule5.11 and distributional duality5.12 can be used separately. No new result inferred from the incorrect sign.

Lemma5.6 has a printed convolution-scale defect and overbroad uniform-convergence wording. Linear weight chi(t)=t needs no such regularization. Literal source preserved; no acceptance based on defective formulas.
